title: I added AI to my gamedev pipeline, here is what I use and how
author: Old_Cartographer7623
selftext:
Hi, solodev here, I'm making this game in which you can sit to reign on the battlefield.

* I started designed the characters with a SDXL model, then I merged some models and I trained my own loras on my characters (all of that is local)
* Then I made several poses and animate with Wan (local too)
* The music is made with Suno (because idk yet a good mocal model but I hope soon)
* I code with Windsurf in Unity Engine, Grok Code Fast coded 60% of the game for free, and the rest is Claude/Gemini/GPTCodex (I'm a real game dev so I check each code line and sometimes I race against the AI to see who'll debug first)
* I use others little AI in my pipeline for generating normal map, removing background, and some 3D gen. That's the point a guy contacted me to work with me and create better hand-crafted 3D assets.

I tested a lot of AI, and I'm happy that I foujd a very good pipeline to produce this entire game, so I launched a kickstarter for people who want to support me and get the game with cool bonus [https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/fireandlight/fire-and-light-thrones-of-tyberion](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/fireandlight/fire-and-light-thrones-of-tyberion)

Feel free to ask me anything!

comments.author: Seven-Prime
comments.body: I'm interested in your first bullet about training models. That'd be something I'd be keen to hear about so I can do some directed research. I'm not at the point yet, but I will be interested in ensure adherence to a 'look.' How did you manage that?

replies.author: Old_Cartographer7623
replies.body:
I keep the style coherence using the same SDXL model with the same custom prompt and loras, for exemple: "black outlines, flat colors, anime"  
And I keep the character coherence building a character Lora model that I can use to do my poses and my artworks.  
So I can now generate this image, then if they are some errors I have skills in digital painting and indrawing.

https://preview.redd.it/gblwmvm7wopg1.png?width=1080&format=png&auto=webp&s=fa5346b581c2ba50901992506808b75073f39250

Tell me if you understand, or if you need a video, I can show you!

comments.author: Adventurous_Win_8692
comments.body:
What's your take on the code quality ai produces?

Im a non coder so im curious how far I can get with the ai coding/debugging alone.

What's your general take on gpt and claude?

From my experience, it seems to get the job done, I do notice they tend to leave fragments of older code behind. 

Otherwise between the models themselves I notice claude tends to be slightly more creative/takes initiative sometimes good sometimes bad where as gpt will general stick to the guidelines

replies.author: SuperHornetFA18
replies.body: Interested in this question as well

replies.author: xhaydnx
replies.body: Not OP, but I would say with good direction it’s great. Sometimes tho when I am lazy and not giving good descriptions of how things should be structured it tends to jumble a lot of things together that should be separate. I don’t think you need to learn to code as much and learn the syntax etc. but you should know how the things connect and where things should go.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: This is the answer, you need to tell it how to do things, not just what to do.  If you're not a coder you may need to do a bit of research about how to approach the type of problem you're trying to solve.

replies.author: Adventurous_Win_8692
replies.body:
Thanks, yeah the way I have it structured at the moment, is somw rules set auch as prioritize resuing code logic instead of recreating, keep things which seem like it should be together grouped, remoce dead/unreachable code when they see it,  referencing GDD, technical doc to get it to speed with the current codespace, changelog, github. 

So far no major issues quite yet, but still early in development

replies.author: pigzyf5
replies.body:
Something that I have found useful, even more so when I am lazy. Is that I have a custom GPT that has all my context. I have it generate my prompts for codex. So in the custom GPT I can put stuff like remember to make it simple, modular, follow best practices and ask if unsure blah blah blah. 
So I don't have to think about that, I ask for the prompt (after going back and forth with design) and it will bake all that in for me

replies.author: ziguslav
replies.body: You can get very far BUT you have to be good at understanding what could go wrong and why. I found that it can code most features I wanted, but sometimes it can go very wrong - at this point I step in and try to see what's happening. Good news is that Claude can eventually find it's own mistakes if you point it in the right direction and are good at describing what's going wrong and when.

replies.author: Old_Cartographer7623
replies.body: It's not my first game, I know the mistakes and I really care about it ;)

replies.author: ziguslav
replies.body: That's good, and I wish you the best, but I was answering to the guy above :P

replies.author: Adventurous_Win_8692
replies.body:
Far as in 80% there? I usually get the other AIs to cross check.

My biggest concern despite all the rules/docs I put in place is the general architecture. How proficient are these bots at building the foundation?

replies.author: ziguslav
replies.body: Well you're not going to build total war, but survivors like or a small strategy? Probably full on thing.

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body: Make a good plan first, document it and execute in chunks. The model itself does not matter that much after that. Claude is not always the best, neither is gemini or codex.

replies.author: srodrigoDev
replies.body: Agree. Making a plan and executing it step by step instead of all at once is the real game changer.

replies.author: Old_Cartographer7623
replies.body:
It's very dangerous to vibe code if you're not a coder.  
But I'm a coder so it's cool.  
In fact I vibe code very little parts of my game to be sure it break nothing. For exemple I never prompt 'make a new power AOE falling from the sky'  
I builded versatile a projectile classe with "fallingFromSky" in input and "AOE" in output, then I prompt "code the AOE area with parametrable size and damage and duration", for a simple request like this "Grok Code Fast" write it for free, and 90% of the time it's good. When it's not good I roll back and retry with GPT / Gemini / Claude.

If it fail again, the probleme is my prompt, so I have to cut the problem into more little pieces and start again ;)
